subject: food-technology
title: Sensory Analysis & Evaluation: Foundations
welcome_lead: Use your senses systematically to judge food — like a scientist with a fork.
meta_desc: GCSE sensory analysis foundations: senses, descriptive words, simple tests.
final_note: A vocabulary of taste is the toolkit of a good evaluator.

concepts.def: Judging food using sight, smell, taste, touch, sound.
How food looks — colour, shape, gloss, garnish.
How food feels — crisp, smooth, chewy.
Combined taste and aroma in the mouth.
Precise word to describe a sensory quality.

walkthroughs.body_html: Sensory analysis uses all five senses: sight, smell, taste, touch and sound. The crunch of celery, the gloss of caramel, the aroma of bread — each gives evidence. Note them in that order: look, smell, listen, feel, taste.

Avoid "nice". Use descriptors — crisp, buttery, tangy, fragrant, bitter, smooth. A good vocabulary list around your cooker turns vague reactions into useful data. Aim for at least three precise words per sense.

Test in a quiet space, with neutral light, cleansing water between samples and identical small portions. Blind tasting (samples coded, no labels visible) avoids bias. Record results immediately — short-term taste memory fades fast.
